title: Measurement Without Validity: The Compounding Reliability Problem in Agentic AI Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2608.00794v5 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Agentic AI evaluation pipelines produce benchmark scores that justify deployment decisions, safety certifications, and regulatory compliance claims. No formal framework has characterized how validity degrades across these stages. We present a knowledge-based three-layer compounding validity model, $V_{\rm total} \leq V_1 \times V_2 \times V_3$, that captures multiplicative degradation across task generation ($V_1$), human-simulator calibration ($V_2$), and automated judgment ($V_3$). Applying it to five widely-used agentic benchmark configurations, we find $V_1$ and $V_2$ independently measurable and both degraded, but $V_3$ not currently quantifiable for any: three of the four benchmarks score with a single deterministic rule, so no second rater exists and reliability is undefined, and the fourth's partial LLM grader has no published grader-vs-human measurement. translated_title: 缺乏效度的测量：智能体AI评估中的复合信度问题
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.00794v5 公告类型：替换 摘要：智能体AI评估流水线所产生的基准测试分数被用于支撑部署决策、安全认证以及监管合规声明，但目前尚无形式化框架刻画效度（validity）如何在这些环节中逐步退化。我们提出了一个基于知识的三层复合效度模型 $V_{\rm total} \leq V_1 \times V_2 \times V_3$，用以刻画效度在任务生成（$V_1$）、人类模拟器校准（$V_2$）和自动评判（$V_3$）三个环节上的乘法式退化。将该模型应用于五种广泛使用的智能体基准测试配置后，我们发现 $V_1$ 和 $V_2$ 均可独立测量且都出现了退化，但 $V_3$ 对任何一个基准目前都无法量化：四个基准中有三个采用单一确定性规则进行评分，因而不存在第二评分者，其信度无从定义；第四个基准所使用的部分LLM评分器也缺乏公开的“评分器—人类”一致性测量。此外，对55篇已发表的智能体评估论文进行的结构化调查发现……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了首个刻画智能体AI评估效度退化的形式化框架——三层复合效度模型（V_total ≤ V1 × V2 × V3），揭示效度在任务生成、人类模拟器校准与自动评判三个环节的乘法式衰减，并实证发现现有主流基准的自动评判环节信度均无法量化，评估体系整体缺乏效度保障。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the first formal framework for validity degradation in agentic AI evaluation—a three-layer compounding model (V_total ≤ V1 × V2 × V3)—showing that validity decays multiplicatively across task generation, human-simulator calibration, and automated judgment, and empirically demonstrates that the reliability of automated judgment remains unquantifiable across widely-used agentic benchmarks.
